title: Unified visibility token filtering for analytics gateway
creator: Marisol Vega
description:
Problem: Analytics endpoints (usage projections, per-route metrics, and aggregated dashboards) currently return data without a consistent enforcement of tenant- and role-level visibility. Multiple surfaces apply ad-hoc filtering which causes subtle leaks (e.g., cross-tenant metric spikes, masked dimensions missing for some callers) and inconsistent query performance. Goal: implement a single, auditable visibility filter layer that enforces RBAC/entitlements for all analytics gateway query paths and for pre-computed usage views while minimizing additional latency and preserving cache effectiveness.

Scope: console backend analytics gateway, materialized usage views (hourly/day aggregations), read APIs used by console dashboards and the Console API. Excludes write-side ingestion pipelines and external export jobs (handled in follow-ups).

Proposed approach:
1) Authoritative policy model: adopt attribute-based access control (ABAC) for analytics surfaces where entitlements are expressed as (role, tenant, org_attribute, metric_mask). Keep role-to-permission mappings in the entitlement service used by Console backends.
2) Visibility layer placement: enforce at the analytics gateway (query-proxy) during plan construction by generating a deterministic WHERE/ROW_FILTER clause so the storage layer (ClickHouse/OLAP) only returns permitted rows. For pre-computed views, apply projection-time masking so materialized tables contain masked columns and a tenant-scoped visibility column.
3) Permission cache: a read-optimized, TTL-backed permission cache co-located with the gateway (LRU + push invalidation on entitlement changes) to avoid a roundtrip per request.
4) Column-level masking: support soft-masking for PII/columns and metric-level suppression (e.g., hide raw token counts for low-privilege roles) implemented as SQL expressions during query rewrite.
5) Consistency guarantees: document and implement eventual consistency surface for entitlement propagation with maximum staleness SLA (30s) and fallbacks for live-critical requests.

Trade-offs considered:
- Query rewrite vs post-filtering: Rewriting pushes filtering to the storage engine which is cheaper on large tables and preserves cache hits; post-filtering is simpler but requires streaming larger result sets and leaks more data to intermediate layers. We chose rewrite for performance and auditability.
- Cache TTL: short TTL reduces exposure window at the cost of cache misses; use 30s TTL with immediate invalidation on entitlement change APIs.
- Complexity: column-level masking increases storage complexity for materialized views; will incrementally roll out masks for high-risk columns first.

Implementation plan / milestones:
- Design doc + policy schema (done)
- Gateway RBAC middleware prototype with query rewrite (spike branch)
- Integrate permission cache and push invalidation hooks
- Add SQL expressions for masking; unit tests + integration tests against test ClickHouse cluster
- Perf run and dashboard of latency/cost impact; gate for release
- Security review + audit logging for every filtered query

Metrics to track: pre/post average query latency (p50/p95), cache hit ratio, percent of requests using masking, number of entitlement changes per hour, correctness signals from synthetic smoke tests.
acceptance_criteria: All analytics gateway query paths apply the deterministic visibility filter resulting in zero rows returned outside tenant/role entitlement in 100% of smoke tests
Permission cache hit ratio >= 95% in steady-state during load tests
p95 query latency increase <= 20% for typical dashboard queries (validated in perf run)
Column masking implemented for three priority PII columns and verified by integration tests
Audit logs include tenant, caller, applied_policy_id and rewrite_hash for every rewritten query
comments: 2025-02-06 - Marisol Vega: Initial triage. Surface reproducer attached to the design doc showing cross-tenant leakage in an edge case when role mapping is missing. Decided to standardize on ABAC rather than ad-hoc role lists.

2025-02-12 - Arjun Patel: Spike complete. Query rewrite approach reduces bytes scanned by ~48% on synthetic 7-day corpus vs post-filtering. Branch: feature/visibility-rewrite. Perf artifacts attached in the PR.

2025-02-18 - Priya Menon (Security): Reviewed masking approach. We need explicit threat model section and requirement that audit logs be immutable; requested an HLD of masking expressions and confirmation of no plaintext dumps in logs.
2025-02-24 - Arjun Patel: Implemented permission cache with Redis-backed store and local LRU; added push invalidation via entitlement webhook. Integration tests for invalidation added.
2025-02-26 - QA (Devon Li): Found flake where queries with unknown metric tags defaulted to permissive filter. Added validation step in policy compiler and unit test to reject unknown tags.

2025-02-28 - PM (Lena Brooks): Confirmed rollout plan; will gate the feature behind a console feature flag and enable for internal orgs first. Also requested a canary dashboard to monitor potential user-facing regressions.
2025-03-01 - Arjun Patel: Submitted PR for review. Perf run attached with results. Requesting security review and owner approval to merge to staging.
2025-03-01 - Security (Priya Menon): Quick pass complete. Need one follow-up: ensure KMS policy for mask keys is scoped to analytics-service role. Marked security_review_required=true.
